leads.name: Treurbeuk, Oude Begraafplaats (Algemene Begraafplaats)
leads.why_lead: Named and dated (circa 1900) by the gemeente/HCL brochure 'Wandelroute Monumentaal Groen' (2022, top-10 entry IV) as standing between sections 2 and 3 of the old cemetery off Spanjaardslaan, with a photo. No matching entry found in the LRMB register within 20km of the city centre, and only a verbal location ('tussen tweede en derde afdeling'), not a coordinate. That path description is close to or the same as lee_004's plane tree location, so a future pass should walk the path and pin both trees individually rather than guess a coordinate from the brochure text alone. One source only; needs a second independent source or a precise coordinate before it can ship.

No LRMB register entry matches this second tree, no coordinate beyond the path/Molenstraat junction, and the species name is truncated in the extracted PDF text (this environment has no pdftotext/PyPDF and text was pulled from raw PDF content streams by regex, which garbles some words). Needs a clean read of the source PDF (or a site visit) to identify the species before it can be verified.

leads.name: Beuk, Rijksscholengemeenschap/Gerechtshof, Zaailand 104
leads.why_lead: LRMB register nr 1682938, planted band 1860-1870, setting 'tuin' (garden). The register's place name combines the old Rijksscholengemeenschap (a 19th-century secondary school on the Zaailand, per nl.wikipedia's Rijks Hogere Burgerschool article, designed by T.A. Romein) with 'Gerechtshof', Leeuwarden's historic Palace of Justice/Court of Appeal building nearby, also a Romein design. The coordinate sits near the modern Zaailand square (redeveloped around 2012 with underground parking) and the Willemskade/Zuiderstraat streets, which OSM shows as ordinary public streets and a pedestrian square with no private-access tags nearby. However, the register's own 'tuin' setting suggests the tree may stand in a courtyard behind the school/courthouse building rather than on the open square itself, and courthouses commonly restrict courtyard access even where the surrounding streets are public. This pass (2026-09-10) could not settle it: an Overpass query for building/amenity tags at the exact coordinate timed out (the host was rate-limiting) and was not retried. Needs either a successful OSM check, a photo showing the tree's actual setting, or a site visit before it can ship either way.

leads.name: Gewone beuk achter De Koperen Tuin, Prinsentuin
leads.why_lead: HCL brochure top-10 entry II, dated 1874, described as having a low branch that limits the height of delivery traffic behind the De Koperen Tuin pavilion in Prinsentuin. Could not be confidently matched to any LRMB register coordinate in Prinsentuin (all register beeches there, nrs 1688389 and 1688418/1688918-equivalent already match the published lee_003 and lee_005); may be a further, distinct beech or may be one of those under a different description. Needs a site visit or a clearer source before publishing to avoid duplicating an already-live tree under a new id.

resolved_2026-09-09.name: Rode paardenkastanjes / Gewone plataan / Witte paardenkastanje, tuin Diakonessenziekenhuis
resolved_2026-09-09.outcome: Shipped as lee_019, lee_020, lee_021. Researched what now occupies the former hospital garden: the Diakonessenhuis closed in 1987 and was converted into apartments in 1988-1990; the garden survives as a landscaped courtyard now named Diaconessenpark. Checked access via OpenStreetMap (Overpass): the courtyard is tagged leisure=park, wheelchair-accessible paved footways run past all three trees, there is a public bench beside them, and no gate or access=private tag exists anywhere in the courtyard (only two low 0.6m garden walls). Judged genuinely open despite two of three register entries listing owner=particulier, and flagged accordingly. See data/research/leeuwarden-verified.json for full verify_notes.

blocked.name: Bruine beuk Princessehof (voorplein)
blocked.reason: LRMB register nr 1682922. The register's own site history: a fungal infection (platte tonderzwam) was found in the mid-1990s and 'Uiteindelijk is de boom in 2015 geveld' (the tree was felled in 2015). A 1 June 1991 letters-page item in 't Kleine Krantsje (HCL archive) independently confirms this was a well-known tree that survived an earlier removal threat in the early 1970s after public protest, but the register's later felling record post-dates that and is more recent evidence. Dead. Do not publish. Not the same tree as the two Sint Anthony Gasthuis entries already blocked.

blocked.name: Bruine beuk, Achtertuin Prinsessenhof (second beech)
blocked.reason: LRMB register nr 1682921, about 14m from the horse chestnut (nr 1682920, blown over in a storm, blocked above) at the same 'achtertuin Prinsessenhof' site. Its own site history is only one line ('De boom stond op een prachtige locatie achter Het Princessehof') using the past tense 'stond', which is ambiguous: Dutch register entries elsewhere in this same file use 'stond'/'staat' inconsistently regardless of whether the tree survives. This pass (2026-09-10) found no independent source confirming this specific beech alive or dead; given two of the three registered trees at this same back garden are confirmed dead (the chestnut blown over, and a beech at the adjoining voorplein felled in 2015), treat this one as uncertain rather than assume it survives. Needs a site check or a newer register read before it can ship either way.
blocked.why_lead: Same as above; keep as a lead rather than blocked outright, since nothing confirms it is dead, only that its neighbours are.

No public path found crossing the site. Treat as private land, not genuinely open, per hard rule 10, unless a future pass finds evidence of a public route through the campus.
